claim: Beat names the scene's job in the plot, and shot size plus intensity fall out of it — a climax automatically gets tighter and louder than a breather without anyone setting either by hand. Directors reach for it to keep a sequence from running at one flat energy for four minutes.
method: identical subject sentence and seed in every panel; only the option clause changes. panels marked control render the untouched subject, because SDXL cannot express absence.

panels.clause: calm, neutral stance, low stakes, unhurried
sudden alert, startled wide eyes, something noticed off-screen
building intensity, determined expression, forward momentum
shock of realization, wide eyes, sharp lighting shift
peak intensity, extreme expression, maximum energy, blazing light
settled calm expression, released tension, soft warm light
wry closing smirk, small final beat, quiet punctuation
relaxed idle moment, low energy, easy breath

review.issue: Two pairs collapse. inciting ("sudden alert, startled wide eyes") and turn ("shock of realization, wide eyes") both reduce to a wide-eyed surprised face. setup ("calm, neutral stance, low stakes, unhurried") and breather ("relaxed idle moment, low energy, easy breath") both reduce to a relaxed neutral boy. "low stakes", "unhurried", "easy breath", "forward momentum" and "something noticed off-screen" are directorial prose that draws nothing.
review.fix: Give each beat one concrete, distinct facial/body tag: inciting -> "surprised, looking to the side, parted lips"; turn -> "wide eyes, backlit, sharp shadow across face"; setup -> "neutral expression, standing, hands at sides"; breather -> "tired smile, hands on knees, catching breath". If two beats cannot be separated on one face, drop one from the renderable set rather than shipping twin panels.
